what: A still frame's time at the worst 1835 stand, per Scene detail tier and release viewport, held as a ceiling beside T-1975's triangle ceilings (DETAIL in renderers/web/js/main.js). Gated by `node tools/measure_still_frame.mjs --gate`; .github/workflows/chicago-4d-frame-time.yml runs it.
unit: milliseconds of one still frame (median of 2, after 2 settle frames), on the machine named: headless Chromium rasterises in software (SwiftShader), so a millisecond is the runner's CPU's and a ceiling belongs to one machine. The gate finds this machine by CPU model and core count; a machine, or a viewport of one, with no number here is read and warned about, never failed on another machine's numbers. The frame is also printed in bare screens (over a frame with every layer hidden, timed in the same page), the first design for a machine-free unit, NOT gated: of three CPUs read on 2026-10-04 two agreed on it within 4 % and the third read it a third higher. docs/measurements/T-2111-still-frame-ceiling.md has the table.
rule: each machine's own reading at the worst stand plus 10 %, rounded up to 250 ms. A parcel that makes every frame slower argues its own numbers here, with its reading, in the same commit; one that makes frames cheaper brings them down to its reading by the same rule.
stand_why: T-2084's back yard on Washington and Wells: the worst 1835 stand at every tier and both viewports in T-2099's table (docs/measurements/T-2099-still-frame.md). 1904's landing is slower still and is T-2109's to fix; this holds 1835.
